title: Grief
hook: grief is love with nowhere to go, and it takes its own time
tomorrow: can you pray for someone whose family isn't religious?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the white pall over the coffin, baptism's white garment at the end of the road. Today, the morning after the funeral.

A second coffee cup set out from habit. A phone number nobody can bring themselves to delete. A voice you still half expect at the door. Is that okay? Yes. People say grief is love with nowhere to go, and it does strange, ordinary things while it looks for somewhere. It also keeps its own time, not anyone else's.
screen: `A SECOND COFFEE CUP.` → `LOVE WITH NOWHERE TO GO.` → `ITS OWN TIME.`

segments.voice: This week walked from the field hospital to the grave. Heal wounds first. Prepare in peace. Food for the way. Jesus, Mary, Joseph. Stay beside. The white pall. Grief comes after all of it. Here's one to tell a friend: one verse in John is only three words long, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "And Jesus wept." He's at the tomb of his friend Lazarus, and in the story he's about to raise him. He weeps anyway. So grief isn't a lack of faith. Paul writes to the Thessalonians about those who have died "that you be not sorrowful, even as others who have no hope." He doesn't say don't grieve. He says grieve with hope. Catholics keep praying for their dead, keep their names, keep a place for them in the Mass. Grief takes its own time because the love didn't end at the funeral. Love continues.
screen: `SIX LINES FROM THE FIELD HOSPITAL TO THE GRAVE.` · `AND JESUS WEPT.` · `GRIEVE, BUT WITH HOPE.` · `NO TIMETABLE.` · then, large: `LOVE CONTINUES.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who is grieving, recently or long ago; old griefs get forgotten by everyone except the one carrying them. Send a short message with their person's name and that you remember. Then let the sit be for them.
Grief. Love with nowhere to go, keeping its own time, and in Catholic hope, still headed somewhere.
Keep this: love continues, the way Jesus wept at the tomb and still called Lazarus out. That's the week.

howItsDone: Catholics grieve with prayer for the dead: Masses offered for them, rosaries said in the days after a funeral, names remembered at Mass and in November, the month of the holy souls.

chat.meaning: Jesus wept at Lazarus's tomb, and Paul says grieve with hope, not don't grieve. Grief is love keeping its own time.

Lazarus.meaning: Jesus's friend, whom he raised from the dead

Thessalonians.meaning: early Christians in Thessalonica, to whom Paul wrote

Paul.meaning: an early apostle who wrote letters to the first churches

Douay-Rheims.meaning: an old English Catholic translation of the Bible

sources.quoted: that you be not sorrowful, even as others who have no hope.

notes: John 11:35 and 1 Thessalonians 4:12 (Douay numbering) quoted from Douay-Rheims (Challoner); confirm exact wording and verse numbers.
'One verse in John is only three words long': counted from the cited Douay text ('And Jesus wept.'); no 'shortest verse' claim.
'People say grief is love with nowhere to go' is presented as a common saying (from the outline), not attributed.
